cases.purpose: Left, right, up, down, Home and End decode as cursor keys: each is followed by x so the deleted character shows where the cursor was.
cases.oracle: Debian 13 vi (vim.tiny 9.1) on the reference PATH as vi; cursor-key bytes chosen by the PTY driver from the DECCKM mode the program selected; file results compared byte for byte. Expected file derived by hand from vi motions: right,right,x -> abdef; End,x -> abde; left,x -> abe; Home,x -> be; down,right,x deletes h on line 2; up,x -> b.
cases.comparison: Exact resulting file. Both builds must produce the independently derived text b / gijkl.

cases.purpose: With TERM=vt100 the program selects its own cursor-key mode; the PTY driver sends the matching bytes, and down,down,dd,right,x edits the right lines.
cases.oracle: Debian 13 vi (vim.tiny 9.1) on the reference PATH as vi; cursor-key bytes chosen by the PTY driver from the DECCKM mode the program selected; file results compared byte for byte. Expected: dd on line 3 leaves one,two,four; right then x deletes the f of four. Hand-derived.
cases.comparison: Exact file text one/two/our; vt100 selects a different key table than the default xterm-256color.
